transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-07
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 mins (recorded)
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Mark Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (CTO, Apollo), Sam Brooks (ML Eng), Jordan Lee (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on PLG/self-serve quickstart and questions around Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, time-to-first-token, free credits, and security considerations for an enterprise pilot. Customer is early production with an internal LLM feature and evaluating options to migrate from trial with faster time-to-first-token and predictable latency/cost.

Topics:
- Quickstart and free credits flow
- Time-to-first-token / integration steps
- Hosted (Redwood API) vs Dedicated vs Private for data residency and compliance
- Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
- Cost/latency tradeoffs and benchmarks

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm lena from redwood, i'll kick us off. Mark who is our se is with me. how are you all doing?
[00:06] Priya: good, thanks. excited to learn more, had a quick internal sync before this.
[00:09] Sam: yeah hi, im sam, i mostly own the model infra at apollo. jordan from ops will chime in for infra questions.
[00:15] Jordan: hey - quick one, timezone stuff, we might need a follow up for APAC tests.
[00:20] Mark: sounds good. quick agenda: talk through the plg quickstart, how fast you can get tokens flowing, then dive into deployment modes if we have time.
[00:28] Priya: perfect. our main goal is to get something in prod within 4-6 weeks if feasible, start with hosted but we need to understand when to move to dedicated or private if data restrictions hit.
[00:38] Lena: totally — that's a common path. for quickstart we provide free credits and a starter template, so you can go from signup to first token in under an hour typically, depending on your infra and auth setup.
[00:48] Sam: under an hour sounds great. what's the friction points usually?
[00:52] Mark: usually oauth/ssso, network policies, and model choice. for example if you want low-latency for short chats you pick a certain family and size. Also caching prefix helps. we have a quickstart repo with examples in node/python.
[01:05] Priya: do you have a demo of the quickstart repo? sometimes these repos assume a lot about infra.
[01:09] Lena: yes i'll send the github link, it's in our docs. the typical flow: create account, redeem credits, api key, try curl or one-line sdk sample — that gets you a first token. then you can add sso and integrate pipelines.
[01:20] Jordan: for hosted, where is data stored? we have residency requirements for EU customers.
[01:24] Mark: hosted endpoints are region-aware; we have EU region and you can pin requests to region. for stricter needs we recommend dedicated or private. private gives you a customer-managed control plane inside your VPC/air-gapped option.
[01:33] Priya: ok, and dedicated is like reserved capacity? we prefer predictable costs.
[01:36] Lena: exactly — dedicated is reserved GPU pools for you, predictable throughput and SLAs. hosted is the fastest path for plg/quickstart.
[01:42] Sam: how long does a dedicated onboarding take?
[01:45] Mark: typically a few weeks for provisioning and capacity planning, sometimes longer if you need on-prem. but you can run the plg quickstart against hosted right away to validate flows and eval model choices.
[01:54] Priya: what about encryption/KMS and audit logs, we need to demonstrate to our security team.
[01:58] Lena: we have kms integrations and full audit logs, plus optional private key management for private deployments. i'll include our security pack with SOC2 and ISO artifacts.
[02:07] Jordan: is sso supported for the console?
[02:09] Mark: yes sso/saml and okta integrations, role-based access controls are in the console.
[02:13] Priya: any gotchas with model variants? we run some heavy embeddings and also generation.
[02:17] Sam: yep embeddings at scale are where we worry about cost.
[02:19] Lena: that's where redwood-optimize suggestions help — we can suggest batching settings and quantized model variants to balance cost/latency. you can also route requests to cheaper variants when quality allows.
[02:30] Priya: do you have examples of per-token cost compared to openai?
[02:33] Mark: we don't publish direct pricing comparisons but we can run a benchmark for you. many customers see material savings with batching and dedicated pricing. we can run a quick benchmark during the follow-up.
[02:43] Sam: would like that, maybe measure latency p95 and cost per 1M tokens.
[02:47] Lena: noted. we'll schedule a performance deep-dive.
[02:50] [02:50] Speaker 1: (overlap) question on fallback policies?
[02:54] Mark: good one — we support smart routing and fallback to compatible model variants or other regions if capacity issues happen. it's part of our reliability controls so your app stays online.
[03:03] Priya: about quickstart, does the free credits expire quickly?
[03:06] Lena: credits typically expire in 60 days; redemption is straightforward and i'll include the exact link in the follow-up.
[03:11] Jordan: for our infra team, can we run a smoke test from our VPC to hosted endpoints? we need to check egress rules.
[03:16] Mark: yes you can. we also have a private deployment option where we deploy into your VPC for strict network policies. But for smoke tests hosted is easiest.
[03:24] Priya: what's your SLA for hosted vs dedicated?
[03:26] Lena: hosted has uptime commitments in the terms, dedicated includes SLA-backed uptime and latency tiers as part of the reserved capacity contract. i'll share the SLA doc.
[03:33] Sam: any limitations on model catalog for hosted? we use a mix of open and proprietary models.
[03:38] Mark: we host curated open models and also support bringing your own model in private/dedicated deployments; hosted model catalog is more curated for performance. BYOM is supported on private/dedicated with additional onboarding.
[03:49] Priya: do you support GPU selection or specific hardware on dedicated? we use A100s in prod today.
[03:54] Mark: yes you can pick hardware profiles for dedicated capacity — that is part of the capacity planning discussion.
[03:58] Lena: quick note — many customers start with our hosted api for first tokens and then move to dedicated once they need throughput/cost predictability or data isolation.
[04:07] Priya: ok that's the path we were thinking. is there a free trial we can use for integration testing?
[04:11] Lena: yes the plg quickstart includes free credits, plus we can whitelist your account for integration testing. i'll confirm exact credit amounts in the email.
[04:19] Sam: nice. also curious about logs and observability — do you expose token-level cost and latency breakdowns?
[04:25] Mark: yes, redwood console has per-route metrics, token-level cost, p50/p95 latencies, traces, and an audit log. you can set alerts on regressions.
[04:33] Jordan: and for compliance we need logging retention options.
[04:35] Lena: we have configurable retention on enterprise plans, i'll include the retention options in the security packet.
[04:41] Priya: timeline wise, if we start the quickstart this week, how soon can we show a POC to product in two weeks?
[04:47] Lena: if you can redeem credits and wire up a simple service to call the api we often see pocs in 1-2 weeks. depends on SSO and approvals.
[04:55] Priya: sounds reasonable.
[04:57] Lena: cool. any final questions?
[05:00] Sam: one minor — you mentioned kv cache and prefix caching? does that work out of the box?
[05:04] Mark: yes we have prefix/KV cache built-in to the runtime and caching policies you can configure; it helps with cost and latency for repeated contexts.
[05:12] Priya: great.
[05:14] Lena: recap / next steps: i'll send the quickstart guide + free credits link, security pack (SOC2/KMS/SAML), and the quickstart repo. Mark will schedule the perf deep-dive to measure p95 and cost per 1M tokens. Priya/Jordan will share expected traffic patterns and infra constraints.
[05:29] Priya: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[05:31] Jordan: thanks all.
[05:33] Lena: thanks, we'll follow up tomorrow with links.

End of transcript.

References & Links mentioned:
